long_biography.plain_text:
Greg Poche began with a railway desk job, worked as a builder's labourer and studied at night before moving into pharmaceutical sales. In 1972, while completing business and operations qualifications part-time, he founded Star Track Express. He spent three decades building the freight company, challenged an industry cartel and ultimately sold the business to Australia Post and Qantas.

After the 2003 sale, Poche and his wife Kay shifted their attention to philanthropy. Their giving helped create a melanoma research and treatment centre, a national network of university-based Indigenous health centres and an Australia-United States cancer-trials partnership. Following Kay's death, those institutions and funds continue their work; their assets remain separate from Poche's private holdings, which are not publicly detailed.
